name: Zulip
tagline: Topic-based chat for teams that work asynchronously
description: Team chat in which every message belongs to a named topic inside a channel. Conversations stay separate and readable, so a day away means skimming a list of topics instead of scrolling one endless stream.
licenseNote: Every server feature is in the open-source build. Self-hosters pay only for optional support and, above 10 users, for the hosted mobile push notification relay, which is free for qualifying community organisations.
backing: Kandra Labs (US), an independent company funded by hosting and support revenue

maturity.rationale: Over a decade in the open, with a careful engineering culture, thorough documentation and a smooth, well-tested upgrade path.

selfHosting.summary: One installer script on a fresh Ubuntu or Debian server sets up the whole stack, certificates included. It expects a dedicated machine rather than a shared one; a Docker image exists but is the less-travelled path.

requirements.notes: 2 GB with swap is the minimum; use 4 GB for a team of more than a hundred.

managedHosting.label: Zulip Cloud
managedHosting.note: Free tier with a limited searchable history; paid plans per user

strengths: Topics make it possible to catch up in minutes and to hold several conversations in one channel
Official importers for Slack, Mattermost and Microsoft Teams
No open-core split: SSO, guest accounts and fine-grained permissions are in the free server
weaknesses: The topic model takes about a week to get used to, and some teams never take to it
The interface is dense and less polished than Slack's
Mobile push for more than 10 self-hosted users needs a paid plan or a community sponsorship
No end-to-end encryption, and calls are handed to Jitsi, BigBlueButton or Zoom rather than built in

featureNotes.mobile-apps: Push notifications are free for up to 10 self-hosted users
featureNotes.calls: One click starts a Jitsi, BigBlueButton or Zoom call
